subject: Problem with latent variable correlating with measured variables

messages.author: 246f8225fbd650b9
messages.subject: Problem with latent variable correlating with measured variables
parts:
Hi all,

I have two latent variables that are made up of ordinal indicators. I'm trying to see how these two latent variables correlate to my measured variables. However, I kept receiving errors when using lavaan. These errors disappear if I define regressions instead of correlations (i.e. "SV + FM + EF ~ CN + AM"). When I tried it in the correlational model in Mplus, it is able to run without any issues. My code is given below. 

model <- 'CN =~ N1 + N3 + N6 + G13 + G7 + G5
AM =~N2 + N4 + G16
SV + FM + EF ~~ CN + AM '
fit <- sem(model, data=data,ordered=c("N1","N3", "N6", "G13","G7", "G5", "N2", "N4", "G16"), estimator="WLSMV"))
summary(fit, standardized=T, fit.measures = TRUE,rsquare=TRUE)

This is the warning message received:
Warning messages:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

2: In lav_model_test(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute scaled test statistic

In addition, the covariances are all zero.
Covariances:
  CN ~~
    SV     0.000                               0.000    0.000
  AM ~~
    SV     0.000                               0.000    0.000
  CN ~~
    FM     0.000                               0.000    0.000
  AM ~~
    FM     0.000                               0.000    0.000
  CN ~~
    EF     0.000                               0.000    0.000
  AM ~~
    EF     0.000                               0.000    0.000

Is there a problem with my model? Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Problem with latent variable correlating with measured variables
parts: I have two latent variables that are made up of ordinal indicators. I'm trying to see how these two latent variables correlate to my measured variables. However, I kept receiving errors when using lavaan. These errors disappear if I define regressions instead of correlations (i.e. "SV + FM + EF ~ CN + AM").

lavaan uses LISREL matrices to represent the model, and there is no matrix for covariances between latent and observed variables.  When you regress the observed outcomes on latent variables, it works because behind the scenes, lavaan creates single-indicator constructs from the observed outcomes, and regresses the "latent" constructs (SV + FM + EF) on the latent predictors (CN + AM).  I suppose a similar automated mechanism is not in place when you try to covary observed and latent variables.  But you can do so in your syntax:

model <- '
  CN =~ N1 + N3 + N6 + G13 + G7 + G5
AM =~N2 + N4 + G16

## create single-indicator constructs to put observed variables in latent space
  SV.lat =~ SV  ## the sem() function automatically fixes residual
  FM.lat =~ FM  ## the variance of single-indicator construct to 0
  EF.lat =~ EF
## covary them
  SV.lat + FM.lat + EF.lat ~~ CN + AM '

Terry
